                         Project Development Objectives
                         Project Development Objective (from Project Appraisal Document)

                         The Project Development Objective is to improve infrastructure services and institutional capacity to support the development of tourism-based economy and cultural
                         heritage circuits in the Kakheti region
                         Has the Project Development Objective been changed since Board Approval of the Project?

                            Yes           No

                         Overall Risk Rating                      Moderate                              Moderate

                         Implementation Status Overview
                         The Project is on track to achieve its development objective. Considerable amount of works have been completed in Telavi, Kvareli and in support of private sector development.
                         Significant results have been achieved to date. Urban regeneration activities have been completed in Telavi and Kvareli, including (i) rehabilitation of municipal infrastructure and
                         utilities in historic city cores; (ii) conservation and upgrading of public spaces, including three public parks in Telavi and one park in Kvareli; and (iii) restoration of 210 building
                         facades and roofs (houses and public buildings) with vernacular architecture in Telavi and Kvareli including interior rehabilitation from damages during the August 2012 storm.
                         Conservation of building facades in the mountainous village of Dartlo has started but is on pause due to winter. Conservation works are completed in Kvareli Castle. At Batonis
                         Tsikhe in Telavi, works have stopped due to the need for design improvement recommended by the Cultural Heritage and Preservation Agency (CHPA), including the proposed


                                                                                                                                                                                                          Page 1 of 5
                             The World Bank                                                                                                                                          Report No: ISR11256



                         museum and conservation plan of the old castle. Construction of tourism facilities at ten cultural heritage sites (Ujarma, Shuamta, Ikalto, Alaverdi, Bodbe, Gurjaani, Akhtala,
                         Ninotsminda, Khirsa, and David Gareji) is underway including: (i) urban landscaping and public parking; (ii) construction of info kiosks, cafes, and public toilets; and (iii) improvement
                         of access roads. The Project has so far leverage about US$8 million of private sector investment directly generated under this subcomponent. Several other private investments
                         have also opened in Kakheti as an indirect result of the Project intervention, whose monetary value is still under surveying and evaluation. The institutional development activities are
Public Disclosure Copy




                         also on track.

                         The overall implementation is assessed as moderately satisfactory as the Project Implementation Entity (MDF) needs to further improve its quality of supervision, contract
                         management and coordination with various agencies involved. The Project Implementation Entity (MDF) has reached agreement with all contractors on specific plans to rectify
                         existing works. Compliance with the design and quality of certain works, especially at cultural heritage sites, needs improvement. Environmental Assessment is assessed as
                         moderately unsatisfactory. Construction waste from rehabilitation works in Telavi and beyond were disposed in a non-acceptable way, between the main road and the river, and
                         remained for an extended period of time. Monitoring and enforcement of environmental management plans (EMP) need considerable improvement. Involuntary Resettlement is
                         assessed as moderately unsatisfactory because progress reporting on Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) is not available.

                         Commitments are at 90 percent, with disbursement at $45.75 million (out of the $60 million), equal to 76 percent of the loan amount.

                         Key Decisions Regarding Implementation
                         An action plan has been agreed with MDF to hire a consulting firm in coordination with the Cultural Heritage and Preservation Agency (CHPA) to fine-tune some design issues at
                         cultural heritage sites and Dartlo village. The MDF has also reached agreement with all contractors on specific plans to rectify existing works that require improvement.
Public Disclosure Copy




                         Restructuring History
                         There has been no restructuring to date.

                         There are no related projects.
